COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the appellants-claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, challenging the judgment and award passed by the Additional District Judge and MACT,
Mysuru in MVC No.854/2010 dated 19.03.2012, seeking enhancement.

entities.text:
Additional District Judge and MACT,
Mysuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief factual matrix leading to the case are that, on 11.05.2007, at 2.30 p.m., respondent No.1 was rider of the two-wheeler bearing registration No.KA-02- EW-8440 and the deceased was a pillion rider.
When they were proceeding near Koramangala Police Station, at that time, the driver of BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA- 01-F-1128 drove it in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result, the bus hit the two-wheeler on which the deceased was traveling as a pillion rider, due to which, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

Hence, the claimants filed the claim petition under Section NC: 2023:KHC:40743 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.30,50,000/- against respondents No.1 to 5.
3.
Respondents No.2 and 5 have contested the claim petition and disputed the liability.
It is asserted that the accident was caused because of actionable negligence on the part of the rider and there is a breach of traffic conditions.
It is also asserted that the rider did not possess a valid driving license and hence, the claim came to be disputed.

The Tribunal after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence on record has awarded a total compensation of Rs.4,18,000/- to the claimants by fastening the liability on respondent No.1 i.e., the owner of the offending two wheeler, on which the deceased was traveling as a pillion rider.
The claim petition as against the other respondents came to be dismissed.
4. Being aggrieved by this judgment and award, the claimants have approached this Court by way of this appeal.

It is also important to note here that the claimants were aggrieved regarding fastening the liability on respondent No.1 alone and they have sought for fastening the liability on respondent No.2- Insurer of the two-wheeler, on which the deceased was traveling as a pillion rider.

No relief was sought against respondents No.3 to 5.
6.
Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants and the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Respondent No.1 though served, did not contest before the Tribunal and before this Court also.

7. The learned counsel for the appellants- claimants would contend that the Tribunal has erred in not fastening the liability on respondent No.2 by passing the Order of pay and recovery, though there is no license to the rider of the motor cycle.

He would also contend that Ex.R3 clearly disclose that it is a package policy and hence, it covers the risk of the pillion rider also and in this NC:
2023:KHC:40743 contest, he invites the attention of the Court to the judgment of the Hon'ble Smt. Kamalamma@Kamala vs V Narayana on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29974151/

3 Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Balakrishnan and Another (Arising out of S.L.P. (Civil) No.1232 of 2012), reported in Civil Appeal No.8163/2012 dated 20.11.2012 and invites the attention of this Court to the Circular dated 16.11.2009 issued by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority and submits that the standard policy and comprehensive/package police are one and the same.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he would assert that the liability can also be fastened on respondents No.3, 4 and 5, in view of the decision reported in AIR 2015 Supreme Court 2261 in Civil Appeal No.4244 of 2015 in the case of Khenyei V/s New India Assurance Company Ltd., and Others.

entities.text: Khenyei V/s New India Assurance Company Ltd., and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He would also contend that the compensation awarded under the various heads was also on lower side and sought for enhancement of the compensation by fastening the liability on the respondents.
Hence, he would seek for allowing the appeal.
Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 would contend that no specific grounds urged regarding pay and recovery.
He would also assert that without there being proper pleadings in the form of grounds of the pay and recovery, the appellants/claimants cannot assert regarding the liability of respondent No.2.
He would also assert that as per Ex.R3, no premium was paid covering the risk of the pillion rider and hence, he would dispute his liability.
He further asserts that respondent No.1, who suffered the award passed by the Tribunal, did not challenge the same and in the appeal also he remained absent.
He would also assert that no declaration is made by the claimants regarding non execution of the award against respondent No.1.
Hence, he would seek for dismissal of the appeal.

9. The learned counsel for respondents No.4 and 5 would support the judgment and further asserts that no relief is claimed as against them, as the relief is claimed only against respondent No.2 and hence, question of fastening the liability against them does not arise at all.
NC: 2023:KHC:40743 10.

It is evident that the deceased Sri. Janakiram was a pillion rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-02-EW-8440, met with an accident near Koramangala Police Station, when it collide with a BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-01-F-1128.
It is also an undisputed fact that the deceased sustained grievous injuries and he succumbed to the injuries.
This fact is again evident from Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.7.
The death of Jayaram in the accident is also evident from Ex.P.8.
The claimant No.1 is examined as P.W.1 and admittedly, she is not an eyewitness to the accident.
Respondent No.3, who was the driver of the BMTC bus is examined as R.W.1 and he disputed actionable negligence on his part.

The Tribunal after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence on record has awarded compensation of Rs.4,18,000/- under various heads as under:

4  CAv QAi RZ 05,000-00 g.U  Loss of dependency 3,78,000-00 g.U  Ml 4,18,000-00 g.U 11.
The Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.3,000/- p.m.

The accident has occurred in the year 2007 and considering the year of the accident, the income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal to the tune of Rs.3,000/- p.m.
cannot be said to be erroneous or arbitrary.
The Tribunal has also applied the multiplier of 14, which is proper, considering the age of the deceased.
However, the Tribunal has not considered or added future prospects.
Admittedly, deceased was self employed and he was aged between 42 to 50 years.

Under such circumstances,
considering the age of the deceased 25% is to be added towards future prospects and hence, the total income of the deceased would be Rs.3,000/- + Rs.750/- =
Rs.3,750/-.
Since there are three dependents - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:40743 to the deceased, 1/3rd is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
As such, 1/3 of Rs.3,750/- works out to (Rs.1,250/- is Rs.3,750-Rs.1,250= Rs.2,500/-)

Hence, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency would worked as follows:
Rs.2,500/- X 12 X 14 = Rs.4,20,000/-
12.
The appellants/claimants are entitled for the compensation under conventional heads of funeral expenses and the loss of estate to the extent of Rs.15,000/- each.
Claimant No.1 is the widow and claimants No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased.
Hence, each of the claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of loss of consortium.

Hence, the claimants are entitled for total compensation under the various heads as under:
1. Loss of dependency Rs.4,20,000/-
2. Loss of consortium (Rs.40,000 x 3) Rs.1,20,000/-
3. Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
4. Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-

5  NC: 2023:KHC:40743 13.

As such the claimants would be entitled for a total compensation of Rs.5,70,000/-
as against Rs.4,18,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
To this extent, appeal needs to be allowed.
14. The appellants/claimants though impleaded the respondents No.3 to 5 in this appeal; he has restricted his claim as against respondent No.2 alone.
Admittedly, the Tribunal has fastened the liability on respondent No.1 on the ground that he did not posses a valid and effective driving license.
The coverage of insurance of offending two-wheeler is undisputed.

In the absence of the valid and effective driving license,
the Tribunal ought to have passed an order of pay and recovery.

15. Though the learned counsel for respondent No.2 contended that there is no specific ground urged in this regard, this Court has got power under Order 41 Rule (2) and under Order 41 Rule 33 of CPC to consider the additional grounds and hence,
by considering the coverage - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:40743 of insurance, pay and recovery possibility needs to be considered.
16.

However, the learned counsel for the appellants has invited the attention of the Court to the decision reported in AIR 2015 Supreme Court 2261 in Civil Appeal No.4244 of 2015 in the case of Khenyei V/s New India Assurance Company Ltd., and Others and argued that, all the respondents are tortfeasors and liability is required to be fastened on all the respondents.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
But, the Tribunal has given its finding to the effect that the accident in question is only because of actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending two wheeler i.e., respondent No.1.
17.
Respondent No.1 did not appear before the Tribunal to contest the matter and also he did not challenge the award passed against him and the award as against him has reached finality.
Now, the appellants- claimants are raising the dispute on behalf of respondent No.1.
When respondent No.1 himself has not challenged - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:40743 the said award, the claimants raising this issue does not arise at all.

18. Further, Ex.P.5- Sketch clearly disclose that the BMTC bus was moving from North towards South on proper side but, the rider of two wheeler has moved from South towards North and after Smt. Kamalamma@Kamala vs V Narayana on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29974151/
6 crossing the middle line, he moved on right side i.e., towards Eastern edge and hit the BMTC bus.
This sketch clearly establishes that the accident is solely because of actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the two-wheeler who moved on wrong side.
Though he was supposed to move on the western edge but, he has crossed the medial line moved on the eastern line, which has resulted in the accident.

The Tribunal has appreciated this aspect in proper prospective and has rightly held that the accident is because of actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the two-wheeler and the said finding does not call for any interference.
Further, the said finding is also not challenged by respondent No.1.
Hence, the said finding cannot be disturbed.
The learned counsel for the appellants/claimants further contended that the liability ought to have been fastened on respondent No.2 by passing an order of pay and recovery.

Ex .R.3 is the policy of the offending two wheeler and it discloses that the premium was paid and though it is a package policy, the premium is paid covering risk of own damages, third party risk and risk of owner cum driver of the offending two wheeler.
No premium is paid, covering the risk of the other passengers or pillion rider.

20. The learned counsel for the appellants- claimants, in this context has placed reliance a decision of the Apex Court reported in Civil Appeal No.8163/2012 in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Balakrishnan and Another (Arising out of S.L.P. (Civil) No.1232 of 2012) and invited the attention of the Court to observation is made in the said decision on para Nos.17, 18 and 19 with reference to the Circular dated 16.11.2009 issued by IRDA to CEOs of all the Insurance Companies, wherein it is clarified that the liability of - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:40743 insurance companies in respect of occupants of a private car and pillion rider on a two-wheeler should be under Standard Motor Package Policy.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Balakrishnan and Another (Arising out of S.L.P. (Civil) No.1232 of 2012)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Based on these observations, it is argued that in the instant case, since it is a package policy, the pillion rider is covered.
However, the said argument cannot be accepted as in the said case the Circular of IRDA has dealt the Standard Motor Package Policy.
21. In the instant case, there is only a package policy pertaining to two-wheeler.
Interestingly, in the instant case under Ex.R.3 separate premium was paid to the tune of Rs.50/- covering the risk of the owner cum driver.
Admittedly, it is a contractual liability and contract under Ex.R.3 disclose that premium is only paid to cover the risk of the driver cum owner.
Admittedly, the deceased was a pillion rider and he does not fall under the category of third party.
No premium was paid covering his risk.

Under such circumstances, the clarification of the above said Circular and the observations in the above said - 16 - Smt. Kamalamma@Kamala vs V Narayana on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29974151/
7 NC: 2023:KHC:40743

decisions will not come to the aid of the appellants- claimants, so as to fasten the liability on respondent No.2.
22.

As regards, respondents No.3 to 5, the evidence clearly disclose that the accident was solely because of actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the two-wheeler and it is not a case of composite negligence or contributory negligence.
Hence, the principles annunciated in the decision reported in AIR 2015 Supreme Court 2261 cannot be made applicable to the facts and circumstances of the case in hand.
Apart from that, even the appeal is restricted to claim the compensation only as against respondent No.2 but, not against other respondents.
Hence, question of considering the liability on respondents No.3 to 5, does not arise at all.
23. Further, respondent No.1, who was the owner of the two-wheeler, did not contest the petition before the Tribunal and before this Court also.
He did not appear so as to contest the matter.
He has not challenged his liability.
Apart from that, there is no declaration filed by - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:40743 the claimants regarding non execution of the award as against respondent No.1.
Further, the Policy does not cover the risk of the pillion rider also.

In view of these facts and circumstances of the case, question of fastening the liability on respondent No.2 does not arise at all and the Tribunal is justified in fastening the liability on respondent No.1 alone.
However, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on lower side and needs to be enhanced.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed-in-part.

(ii) The claimants are entitled for total  compensation of Rs.5,70,000/- as  against Rs.4,18,000/- awarded by the  Tribunal.
 (iii) The enhanced compensation of Rs.1,52,000/- shall carry interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition till the date of payment.
(iv) The entire liability is fastened on respondent No.1-owner of the two-wheeler.

8
(v) The appeal as against respondents No.2 to 5 stands dismissed.
